result.topic_en: Gauss describes tetrahedral (barycentric-type) coordinates of a point relative to a given tetrahedron, with a formula for the squared distance between two points, and then states a fundamental law of crystallisation as a rational-ratio relation among products of sines of the angles between the normals of five crystal faces.

methods.what: Tetrahedral coordinates of a point relative to an origin, defined as signed distances to planes parallel to the faces divided by the altitudes, summing to zero
Squared distance between two points expressed in tetrahedral coordinates and the edge lengths of the tetrahedron
Law of rational indices for crystals: for five face normals on the sphere, products of sines of the arcs between pairs stand in a rational ratio
Linear (Ptolemy/Plücker-type) identity among the three sine products
Coordinate form of the crystallisation law using 2x2 determinants of the normals' coordinates, with the fifth point at (0,0,1)
